synthNotes:
HEADLINE FIRST: every source in this catalogue measures generated prose in FICTION, verse, essays, news or speeches; none measured the archival, chronicle or encyclopedic register the dossier rules govern — say so in the first paragraph, mark every rule that rests on fiction-only evidence, and let the record-register angle's findings (if any landed) stand as their own section. ADD A MODEL-ERA COLUMN to every feature (model and date observed: Schifano Oct 2023, Dramatron 2022, Akoury GPT-4 2023, Church's '250 words' pre-2024 and plainly false of 2026 models, the Nvidia demo May 2023, Cobey ChatGPT-3.5, Williams Jan 2024, Hockaday Oct 2023, beside StoryScope, Sui, Hamilton and Narrative Flattening 2026) and re-weight rules that rest only on pre-2024 observations. RE-CUT these claims to their supported limbs when you cite them: [25] as '10.7% and 8.9% of the total range of similarity scores' (then feature 25 stops resting on the press release [252] — retire [252]); [30] without the emotion-word sign (it then supports features 10 and 19); [223] from the Ngram passage; [238] naming the 'advanced technical language' prompt; [60] to the clichés and learn-with-exposure limbs only; drop [97] and [142]. RECONCILE the previous critic's contradictions: fragments are banned by feature 12 (tropes.fyi, Jones, Negrek) while Vollmer's tell #12 on the same page says 'no fragments' is the tell — state both and resolve by model era or by register; feature 2 ('ends, then ends again') and feature 20 (Dramatron: 'the stories do not finish') point opposite ways — model era again; feature 18 puts Makin [184] in the 'it is a tell' camp although [184] says the tell has drifted; feature 15's single-source flag beside Reinhart [33] — count two, one partial; fix the miscounted 'Supported by' headers (script the recount from the JSON), the StoryScope row count (15 or 17, not nine or 13), and the citation convention breach in feature 9 ([78]'s rejected figure) and feature 18 ([225]). COPYRIGHT: in five bullets the quotation stops and the sentence continues with the source's next words unquoted ([108], [133], [186], [189], [181]) — paraphrase the tails. Single-source features beyond the five flagged: 12, 2's 'ends again', 5, 8, 13, 16, 17, 19, 20, 26, and 3's second clause (the section's inference) — flag each. Then the register map: which failure modes bind the dossier, which the Herald, which the DM page.

R9 SYNTHESIS (the ARCHIVAL round): a new Part with a two-column table per fault — measured in the ARCHIVAL / encyclopedic / gazetteer / biographical-record register, or only in fiction and news — so the constraints the dossier's registers actually need are stated as constraints (what our record prose must not become), not as style advice; the decoding literature as the MECHANISM section under features 5, 11, 17 and 31; the second tell catalogue set beside the Wikipedia guide with each tell's source; the community and reviewer voices on generated SETTING prose as their own feature; MODEL ERA on every new row. No quotation over twelve words.

extraAngles.prompt: THE DOSSIER'S OWN REGISTER IN THE WILD — worldbuilding and TTRPG setting prose under AI (zero rows so far): r/worldbuilding's and r/DnDBehindTheScreen's AI-content rules and moderator posts (2022–2026) and what they say generated SETTING text does wrong; World Anvil, Kanka, LegendKeeper and Obsidian Portal blog and policy pages on AI text; DMs Guild and DriveThruRPG AI-written setting supplements and their one-star reviews (the reviewers' own words about the prose); Rascal News, Polygon and Dicebreaker coverage of AI text in TTRPG publishing (2023–2026); any reviewer who read a GENERATED setting book or gazetteer rather than a generated module. CLAIMS: what readers of setting and gazetteer prose say the AI tell IS in that register — one limb each, a quote under twelve words, the speaker named (a moderator, a reviewer, a publisher), modelEra where stated.

GAZETTEER, TRAVEL AND LOCAL-HISTORY PROSE UNDER AI, MEASURED OR REVIEWED: the New York Times investigation of AI-written travel guidebooks on Amazon (Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, August 2023 — its Originality.ai testing and the sample guidebook prose it quotes); Wikivoyage's AI-content policy and the cleanup discussions on its pub and talk pages; Slate on the Arcadia-style AI local-history books (the record-register finder noted it and did not fetch); Lonely Planet's and TripAdvisor's generated-summary reception; any library, archive or historical-society statement on AI-written local history. CLAIMS: the specific faults named in PLACE-describing prose (generic superlatives, the missing particular, the evaluative close, invented facts, the identical opener across entries), each with speaker, source and modelEra.

THE BIOGRAPHICAL RECORD UNDER AI (two genealogy practitioners carry the whole register so far): The Verge (Mia Sato, February 2024) and Wired's follow-up on AI obituary spam and what the generated obituaries got wrong in the record register; Judy G. Russell (The Legal Genealogist) on ChatGPT-fabricated citations; WikiTree's and FamilySearch's AI policies and their stated reasons; Find a Grave generated-biography complaints. CLAIMS: the faults of generated biographical RECORD prose (invented kin, hedged dates, the eulogy register leaking into the record, fabricated citations), each sourced with modelEra.

HISTORICAL FACT UNDER MEASUREMENT (no row tests a model on dates or events): the HiST-LLM / Seshat Global History Databank benchmark (del Rio-Chanona, Turchin et al., NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks; the January 2025 reporting with GPT-4 Turbo near 46 percent) — the paper's own figures by period and region; the ASIC summarisation trial's PRIMARY (the Australian Senate answer to questions on notice on aph.gov.au) rather than the paywalled Crikey headline [336]; the ABC article via a Wayback id_ capture (the finder's URL landed on a weather story). CLAIMS: measured accuracy of models on dated historical facts and archival summaries, with the instrument, the figure and the model era.

THE DECODING LITERATURE BEHIND THE METRONOME AND THE LOOP (cited inside two verifier notes, never as a row): Holtzman, Buys, Du, Forbes and Choi, 'The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration' (ICLR 2020) — the measurement that human text is bursty in surprisal and machine text flat, the floor under features 5, 11 and 17; Meister, Pimentel, Wiher and Cotterell, 'Locally Typical Sampling' (TACL 2023); Nguyen et al., 'Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling' (ICLR 2025) — a peer-reviewed claim that high temperature can be made coherent, which feature 31's temperature verdict must answer; Mirostat; contrastive search; Sam Paech's slop-forensics and antislop sampler as a primary (present only as a forum relay in partial row 197). CLAIMS: the measured mechanism (surprisal flatness, repetition loops, the entropy of sampled text) and what each sampler changes, with the paper's own figures and the model era.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT RECORD-REGISTER TELL CATALOGUE (feature 29 and every [R] tag rest on one Wikipedia page family): Pangram Labs' 2025 analysis of AI text on Wikipedia; the CSD G15 speedy-deletion criterion and its August 2025 RfC — the community's operative tell list written to be enforced, in its exact wording; the French Wikipedia Observatoire des IA and the German counterpart project pages; the Cornell Tech source-quality analysis of Grokipedia (Triedman et al., November 2025) beside Yasseri; and the peer-reviewed measurements the section asserts second-hand — Herbold et al. 2023 (Scientific Reports: ChatGPT essays rated higher; nominal density and sentence complexity measured), Guo et al. 2023 HC3 (the first published tell list), Jentzsch and Kersting 2023 (90 percent of 1,008 jokes were 25 jokes), Naous et al. 2024 (cultural defaults), Mohammadi 2024 (RLHF diversity loss), Yakura et al. 2024 (the Max Planck spoken-language study, present only as Kriss's relay [916]), Chambers and Kelley 2025 (autistic writing misclassified — verify by Crossref DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-98420-4_7). CLAIMS: each catalogue's tells in the ARCHIVAL or encyclopedic register with the measured figure, and each paper's own measurement, with model era.
